findings: Recent masters use dark centered explanatory objects and stable headings. Dark lighting alone cannot solve this V1 correction.
OhioV2 demonstrates spatial continuity and consequence; VoyagerV2 demonstrates complete connections and mobile geometry inspection. Neither imposes its palette or panel layout.
V1 made a new palette but retained distant mannequin, long diagram and fixed upper labels. Its direction promises exceeded realized motion and tactile involvement.

alternatives.resolution: Rejected: preserves the static construction and weak opening/ending.

alternatives.treatment: Original macro contact film with anticipated-contact overlay
alternatives.resolution: Selected: same physical event carries movement, forecast, contact and remaining sensation; close framing and lighting serve tactile comprehension.

alternatives.treatment: Generated realistic actors and brain fly-through
alternatives.resolution: Rejected: temporal hand continuity and unsupported neuroanatomical precision would weaken truthful explanation.

application: First two seconds inspect real contact/reaction states with captions muted.
Prediction must appear at the future contact site before the moving hand arrives.
Preserve nonzero touch, robot-origin control and clearly visible delayed-follow contrast.
End repeats opening self-touch after viewer has learned what the forecast means.
limits: Sampled overview/phone inspection is not continuous watching, subjective listening or native feed QA.

findings: Mirror uses a warm portrait, fixed headings and separate eye/retina panels; strong identity, mostly flat vector depth.
Roadster preserves car identity and changes force consequences; dark mechanical stage and repeated headings.
Ohio uses original archive and oblique spatial rescue; cause and consequence visibly progress.
Voyager retains failed memory identity and complete connections; explanatory panels risk static repetition.
